title: Playwright quizzes
intro: Short checks on the stack I use at work. After you pick an answer, I show why. Notes and spoken Q&A are still on their own pages.

options: To skip the login UI in every test and reuse cookies / storage.
To run tests in Safari only.
items.why: I log in once, save the session, then tests start already authenticated.

items.q: What belongs in a Playwright fixture?
options: Setup the test needs: page, user, API context.
items.why: Pages hold locators. Fixtures hold setup. Tests stay short.

items.q: Which locator is usually more stable?
items.why: Role + name is close to the user. Generated CSS classes break often.

options: The business result: user created, status 201, cart TOTAL.
The test took less than 30 seconds.
items.why: I check the outcome, not only the click path.

items.q: A test is flaky. What do you do first?
options: Look at locators, timing, data, environment, and the trace.
Run it 50 times and ignore it.
items.why: Sleep hides the cause. Trace and data usually show it.

items.q: When do you use one worker?
options: When tests share an account or a cart.
items.why: Shared state plus parallel = flake. Independent tests can run in parallel.
APIRequest is the Playwright way. I used REST Assured in Java before.

items.q: Smoke on a pull request should be…
options: Small and fast, critical paths only.
items.why: PR jobs must be short. Nightly can be wider.

footer: Mykhailo Kovalenko · Senior General QA Engineer
